sections.html:
Warren County is in south central Iowa, inside the Des Moines metropolitan area, with Indianola as the county seat. It borders Polk to the north, Marion to the east, Lucas to the southeast, Clarke to the southwest and Madison to the west. About 52.9 percent of residents live in urban areas, and 80.2 percent of occupied housing units are owner-occupied.

The county had 52,403 residents in 2020 and an estimated 57,331 in 2025, growth of 13.4 percent over the prior decade. Indianola had 15,833 people in 2020, Norwalk 12,799 and Carlisle 4,160. Parts of Des Moines and West Des Moines also lie inside the county lines, so a house with a West Des Moines or Des Moines mailing address can still be taxed here. Check the parcel.

Indianola is a college and balloon town about 19 miles south of downtown Des Moines, home to Simpson College and the National Balloon Classic each summer. Iowa Highway 92 crosses the city and meets US 65 and 69 southeast of downtown. The Indianola Community School District runs four elementary schools, a middle school and a high school.

Indianola requires rental owners to register and have rentals inspected every two years. A seller with a rented house should confirm its certificate with Code Enforcement at 515-962-5275.

Norwalk grew through annexations and new subdivisions at the edge of the metro, from 6,884 people in 2000 to 12,799 in 2020, with an estimated 15,004 in 2025. Michael Foods is building an $85 million distribution center there. Carlisle sits between the North and Middle rivers and grew from 3,497 residents in 2000 to 4,160 in 2020. Fast-growing towns mean a lot of newer houses, so a seller of an older home competes with recent builds.

The county's main offices are in the Administration Building at 301 N. Buxton Street in Indianola. The Warren County Justice Center opened in summer 2022.

  • Treasurer: Suite 102, 515-690-9240, propertytax@warrencountyia.org. Hours are 7:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. Monday through Friday. Call ahead, since service is by appointment.
  • Assessor: Suite 108, 515-690-9170, assessor@warrencountyia.org.
  • Recorder: Suite 109, 515-690-9110, recorder@warrencountyia.org. The Declaration of Value form and a transfer tax calculator are linked on the county site.

Property tax can be paid online through iowatreasurers.org, where Warren County is county ID 91.

The assessor sets value at 100 percent of fair market value as of January 1, before any state rollback factor is applied, and revalues real property every two years.

  • An informal review with the assessor is open April 2 through April 25.
  • A written Board of Review protest is open April 2 through April 30, limited to the grounds in Iowa Code 441.37.
  • In odd-numbered equalization years, notices are due by October 8. Protests of equalization changes are taken October 9 through October 31, and the Board sits October 10 through November 15.

The assessor does not collect tax or set rates. The treasurer collects, and the taxing bodies set levies after public hearings. The county site links forms for the homestead credit, military exemption, disabled veteran credit and family farm.

The fiscal 2027 county levy is 5.64659 per $1,000 of taxable value for urban property and 8.38166 for rural property, down 3.36 and 2.80 percent from fiscal 2026. The residential rollback, which turns assessed value into taxable value, is 44.5345 percent against 47.4316 percent the year before. Residential property makes up 87 percent of assessed value and 80 percent of taxable value in the county.

sections.h2: Due dates and what happens at closing
sections.html:
Property tax is paid in two halves, the first due September 1 and the second March 1. Late interest of 1.5 percent is added on the first of each month after the grace date.

In an ordinary sale, taxes are prorated and the buyer is credited with the seller's share, which the settlement statement should show. Unpaid city utility or service charges can also be certified to the county treasurer and collected like taxes, so a title company will look for them.

Transfers carry Iowa's real estate transfer tax of 80 cents for each $500 above the first $500, owed by the seller under Iowa Code 428A.3. The recorder will not record a taxable deed until it is paid.

The county holds an online tax sale each June on the GovEase platform, and the delinquent list is published in The Carlisle Citizen beforehand.

  • Owners are notified within 15 days of the sale.
  • Redemption costs the sale amount plus 2 percent a month, with each part of a month counted as a whole month.
  • A 90-day redemption notice can be issued after 1 year and 9 months for a regular sale, or after 9 months for a public bidder sale.
  • Fees include $20 for a certificate and $25 for a treasurer's deed.

If your parcel has already been sold at tax sale, get a redemption figure from the treasurer before planning a closing.

We buy Warren County houses as-is, including houses with delinquent taxes, a tax sale certificate or an unpaid utility lien. Send the address and the tax statement, and we reply with a written offer. That gives you a number to set beside the redemption amount and your own plans.

At closing the title company pays off taxes, redemption amounts and liens from the proceeds, and you receive what is left. Ask the treasurer for a written payoff before you pick a date, and ask Code Enforcement or the city about any rental certificate if the house is rented.

faqs.q: What is the county seat of Warren County, Iowa?
faqs.a: Indianola, with 15,833 residents in 2020. The county administration offices are at 301 N. Buxton Street.

faqs.q: How do I protest a Warren County assessment?
faqs.a: Ask the assessor for an informal review between April 2 and April 25, or file a written Board of Review protest between April 2 and April 30. The grounds are listed in Iowa Code 441.37.

faqs.q: Which Warren County school district has the highest levy?
faqs.a: For fiscal 2027, Carlisle at 17.22926 per $1,000, followed by Indianola at 17.11308. Pleasantville is lowest at 14.19761.

faqs.q: How is the residential rollback changing in Warren County?
faqs.a: The fiscal 2027 residential rollback is 44.5345 percent, down from 47.4316 percent in fiscal 2026. A lower rollback means a smaller share of assessed value is taxed.

faqs.q: What does it cost to redeem a Warren County tax sale parcel?
faqs.a: The owner pays the sale amount plus 2 percent per month, counting any part of a month as a full month, plus a $20 certificate fee. Call the treasurer at 515-690-9240 for an exact payoff.
